81704.subject: The Americans changing politics for the better
81704.body:
The Economist Picks

Автор: The Economist

Прочитати на LinkedIn
https://www.linkedin.com/comm/pulse/americans-changing-politics-better-the-economist-rieve?lipi=urn%3Ali%3Apage%3Aemail_email_series_follow_newsletter_02%3BRCq1QFqHSuuQ283gX7KpNA%3D%3D&midToken=AQFTjFOONAfT2w&midSig=2xxvtFx1jU5Yw1&trk=eml-email_series_follow_newsletter_02-null-0-read_more_banner_cta_&trkEmail=eml-email_series_follow_newsletter_02-null-0-read_more_banner_cta_-null-fz96fz~mvuxwr48~nl-null-null&eid=fz96fz-mvuxwr48-nl
  
In February I was on a building site in Texas. The bosses and workers I spoke to, who were nearly all Hispanic, were unhappy. Many had voted for Donald Trump in 2024, believing he was a successful businessman who would be good for the economy. They also hoped he would do something sensible about disorder on the border. They were sorely disappointed.  Instead of rounding up the “worst of the worst”, as he had promised, Mr Trump sent ICE agents to round up everyone they thought might be an illegal immigrant. In Texas that included anyone who looked Latino and had tools in their truck. Mass deportation devastated the construction business in South Texas. Jobs were taking twice as long because workers were scared to come to work. One boss told me of ICE grabbing people halfway through pouring concrete, ruining the job and costing his small firm $20,000.  At the time I wrote: “Latino disenchantment could decide the midterms.” Our cover package this week suggests that may indeed happen. Hispanics and Asians are the swing-iest voters, and have swung sharply away from Mr Trump. This has implications that go beyond next week’s crucial elections. Unlike the most tribal voters, whose views on transgender issues reliably and illogically predict their views on Iran, Latino and Asian voters tend to think for themselves. Neither party can take them for granted, and they care most about bread-and-butter issues, such as the economy. This is bad news for Mr Trump, but excellent news for American democracy, which needs less shrill partisanship and more problem-solving.  In Britain and Europe our cover is on Andy Burnham’s first budget. The Labour prime minister’s chancellor, John Healey, presented a platter of small measures, such as handouts to help with heating bills, that spooked neither the bond market nor his party’s backbenchers. But most of the big, difficult stuff has been put off until a later date. Britain needs faster growth, more houses and serious work to prepare for the changes that AI may bring. Treading water is not good enough.  On The Insider this week we ask whether America’s midterms will make the world more dangerous. If Mr Trump is constrained at home by a Democratic Congress, will he throw his weight around abroad? You can watch it now.  Robert Guest, Deputy editor Enjoying this newsletter?
